q1: Compared 490 races from 1994–2024 with both front-row definitions observed; excluded 87 races with incomplete front-row support. Recorded nonstarters are removed before eligibility is checked (138 driver entries in this window). 1994–2013 Grid 1–2: Suzuka Circuit, 76.9% (20/26); 1994–2013 Qualifying 1–2: Suzuka Circuit, 76.9% (20/26); 2014–2024 Grid 1–2: Yas Marina Circuit, 86.4% (19/22); 2014–2024 Qualifying 1–2: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, 81.8% (18/22). Ranks are descriptive, with ties and wide intervals possible; changes cannot be attributed causally to hybrid regulations.

q3: 2014–2021: Lotus F1 has the highest supported strict rate, 17.3% (13/75), 95% Wilson interval 10.4%–27.4%; the broad-map leader is Lotus F1 (24.0%); 2022–2024: Alfa Romeo has the highest supported strict rate, 12.5% (11/88), 95% Wilson interval 7.1%–21.0%; the broad-map leader is Alfa Romeo (12.5%). Excluded 28 recorded nonstarters from both numerator and denominator. Withdrawal/nonqualifying labels exclude only entries without positive laps; positive-lap withdrawals remain starts. Both cause maps require laps below winner distance as an early-end proxy; 1 full-distance component-status row(s) are flagged and excluded from both retirement numerators, while remaining in the start denominator. 10 remaining zero-lap mechanical/ambiguous rows have uncertain start status; the exported table reports a sensitivity excluding these. The numerator excludes explicit crash/damage, driver-health and regulatory outcomes while these started entries remain in the denominator. Rankings use at least 40 starts and recorded constructor IDs, so a rename does not automatically inherit its predecessor's rate. Wilson intervals and unequal exposure mean that the largest observed rate is not necessarily evidence of the least reliable constructor.
